ring: everything else that touches a goal
focus: root instructions, repo rules, hook hub + shared flags, env rosters, feature catalogues, per-CLI goal playbooks, scaffold metadata, retrieval conventions, dist parity
sourcesRead: system-spec-kit: ENV-REFERENCE.md, hook-system.md, quick-reference.md, retrieval-conventions.md, template-guide.md, folder-structure.md, templates/README.md, EXTENSION-GUIDE.md, create.sh, template-structure.js, graph-metadata-parser.ts, check-template-staleness.sh, dist validator+resolver, dist-freshness.cjs, scaffold-golden-snapshots + template-version-parity + spec-doc-structure tests, feature-catalog, manual-testing-playbook 454, leaf-manifest.json
cli-external-orchestration: feature-catalog, manual-testing-playbook root CE-P03, six per-CLI goal-hook playbooks
novelty: Ring 4 resolves all four ring-3 questions (hub-row ownership: three hand-maintained rosters agree; dist: in step and freshness-gated; root rules: posture only, zero goal mentions; catalogues: accurate in the large but six defects). It produces eight confirmed defects, downgrades R1-F1 to local drift plus a misleading rule statement, and names the four-way vocabulary collision on the word goal.

label: /goal resume reactivates three statuses in the plugin and two in both catalogues, while the core refuses two of them
detail: Plugin resumeGoal passes allowedFrom ['paused','usage_limited','budget_limited'] and the transition map independently grants usage_limited->active and budget_limited->active. Both feature catalogues say resume reactivates only paused or usage_limited. The runtime-neutral core throws INVALID_STATUS_TRANSITION unless status is paused. Three surfaces, three behaviours for one verb; nobody documents the core's stricter rule, and the core can never reach the two extra statuses because its VALID_STATUSES set is active|paused|completed|cleared.

label: Two goal engines with incompatible status vocabularies and no mapping: completed vs complete, plus surface-specific cleared/blocked/usage_limited/budget_limited
detail: Core statuses are active|paused|completed|cleared, documented in the engine README's injection sentence. Plugin statuses are active|paused|blocked|usage_limited|budget_limited|complete, documented in goal-opencode.md's argument-hint and the plugin catalogs/playbook. completed and complete name the same operator concept with different strings; cleared, blocked, usage_limited and budget_limited are each surface-specific with no cross-reference. bin/goal.cjs show prints status=completed where /goal show prints status=complete.

label: CC-029 and its benchmark evidence rest on a constitutional rule file that no longer exists
detail: A path .opencode/skills/system-spec-kit/constitutional/goal-prompting-runtime-specific.md is cited as CC-029's constitutional routing authority in the playbook and in four benchmark record files including the JSON constitutionalRuleRel field. system-spec-kit has no constitutional/ directory and a repo-wide name search finds only the citations. Provenance INFERRED from a .git/lost-found object that once held the file's text (a runtime-specific rule about the /goal -> /opencode_goal rename). Settling action: restore the file or repoint the citations at the goal_prompting block of speckit-plan.yaml, which the sentence actually names.

label: CL-007's evidence cites a command filename that does not exist (goal_opencode.md) while its quoted lines match the real hyphen file exactly
detail: The playbook cites .opencode/commands/goal_opencode.md (underscore) four times, including 'Command file read confirmed ... exists', but the real file is goal-opencode.md. Every quoted line number and string (4 allowed-tools, 15 the state-free router sentence, 37 the never-reads-state sentence, 39 empty-arguments routing) matches the hyphen file exactly, so only the citation path is stale. The old spelling survives in deep-loop benchmark fixtures, consistent with a rename that left citations behind.

label: CO-039 pins seven suites and 125 tests; the glob matches eight suites and this run reports 137/137
detail: CO-039 says 'the 7 opencode-goal-*.test.cjs suites exist' and 'the focused suite passes 125/125'. Observed in this iteration: the glob matches 8 files and node --test .opencode/plugins/tests/opencode-goal-*.test.cjs reports tests 137 / pass 137 / fail 0. The playbook's pass criterion cannot be satisfied as written and nothing regenerates its numbers.

label: plugins/README.md states a per-concern kill-switch rule that computes to the dead name SYSTEM_GOAL_DISABLED for goal
detail: plugins/README.md gives the model as per-concern SYSTEM_<CONCERN>_DISABLED=1 with two SYSTEM_* examples, and lists OPENCODE_GOAL_PLUGIN_DISABLED only among 'Legacy / plugin-specific aliases'. The true model is the inverse: goal is one of six CONCERN_CANONICAL concerns whose canonical name OPENCODE_GOAL_DISABLED is hand-set and test-pinned; OPENCODE_GOAL_PLUGIN_DISABLED is its alias. Applying the printed rule yields SYSTEM_GOAL_DISABLED, the exact dead name in the operator's local hook-flags.env:25 (R1-F1, now downgraded). Three other rosters (hub table, shared README, ENV-REFERENCE) state the pair correctly.

label: The root README promises injection on every turn; Cursor's only delivery is sessionStart
detail: README.md:861 says the runtime injects the durable slice on every turn. True for OpenCode (transform), Pi (input) and Devin (SessionStart + UserPromptSubmit), but Cursor registers one delivery point, sessionStart, and the injection contract states beforeSubmitPrompt never delivers and stop never fires. retrieval-conventions.md:282 excludes the root README from both retrieval lanes, so nothing downstream corrects the reader.

label: README's 'a parent goal' narrows the manifest's 'phase parents and top-level packets' scope
detail: The public README sentence reads 'a parent goal warns past 3,000 characters and fails past 4,000' while the manifest scopes the budget to phase parents and top-level packets. A plain top-level packet is not a phase parent, so the README can read as excluding it. It is the only budget sentence outside the skill.

label: PI-021 expects the legacy filename shape pi-<sha256>.json for fresh scoped state
detail: PI-021's expected signals name two opaque pi-<sha256>.json files. A fresh scope writes <sha256-of-[workspace,runtime,sessionId]>.json; pi-<sessionDigest>.json is only the legacy adoption name used when the state dir is the workspace default. An operator validating the playbook by looking for pi-*.json after a fresh set finds none and could record a false FAIL.

label: The word goal names four unrelated things in this repository and no document disambiguates them
detail: (1) the session-goal system; (2) ordinary prose and feature labels (README Goal bullet, sk-git table column); (3) goal-file-manifest.txt, a deep-review scope manifest parsed as repo-relative paths, documented nowhere else in the live tree and unrelated to goal.md; (4) ClickUp product goals, whose card self-declares Capability status UNSUPPORTED. A grep for goal interleaves all four.

label: CE-P03 explains injection-only as 'prompt surfaces do not receive the hook's native session id'; the hooks do, the command does not
detail: CE-P03's causal clause misplaces the reason: cursor/goal-inject.mjs resolves payload.session_id with conversation_id fallback and both adapters write a turn touch, so the hooks have identity and write. What lacks identity is the command surface, which fails closed with UNSUPPORTED_SESSION_BINDING, as CU-027 states correctly. Extends the R1-F5 injection-only wording cluster to a second document.

question: Who owns the hooks hub coverage row, and does the same table exist elsewhere that could drift?
answer: The row is hand-maintained in .opencode/hooks/README.md (concern table :50, matrix :230-240, tree :135-142, sibling note :24) and restated independently in hooks/shared/README.md:88 and runtime/ENV-REFERENCE.md:83. The three agree today; nothing generates the hub table from hook-flags.cjs, whose test pins guard the resolver rather than the prose. The drift failure mode is already visible in plugins/README.md:96-98 (R4-F6).

question: Is runtime/dist/lib/validation/spec-doc-structure.js in step with the hand-written .ts carrying budgetApplies?
answer: In step and freshness-gated. dist/lib/validation/spec-doc-structure.js:853, :858, :863 carry isPhaseChildFolder and budgetApplies; dist/lib/templates/level-contract-resolver.js:192-199 carries the goalDurableBudget validation. validate.sh:26 runs the orchestrator from dist and validate.sh:29 consults cli/lib/dist-freshness.cjs, which compares source hashes and exits 69 on stale dist. Ring 3's finding therefore describes shipped behaviour.

question: Do root instruction files and repo rules restate the budget, the resend rule or the offer in words that could drift from ring 3?
answer: No. REPO RULES.md and all eleven repo-rules/*.md contain zero goal mentions. AGENTS.md:291-297 restates only the posture and delegates mechanics explicitly at :297; its posture lines match the slice module's frontmatter boundary and resendPending's hash semantics. Numbers, flags and channels appear only in README.md:861-866, where R4-F7 and R4-F8 find the two imprecisions.

question: Do the feature catalogues and manual-testing playbooks describe the phase-child budget correctly and name the right disable flag?
answer: Neither: the catalogues and playbooks do not describe the budget at all, so ring 3's contradiction stays confined to validation-rules.md and goal-set-string-playbook.md versus the hook. Six other defects were found in them instead (R4-F1, F3, F4, F5, F9, F11). The two playbooks that exercise the disable path (DV-022, CU-027 rollback) teach the alias OPENCODE_GOAL_PLUGIN_DISABLED, which works but keeps the alias in circulation as the primary switch.

text: The dead SYSTEM_GOAL_DISABLED line is local-only drift, not a shipped defect: git check-ignore confirms .opencode/hooks/hook-flags.env is ignored (.gitignore:287) and the committed hook-flags.env.example:25 carries the canonical OPENCODE_GOAL_DISABLED, which hook-flags.test.cjs:38 pins. What remains is the misleading rule statement in plugins/README.md:96-98 (R4-F6) that would still send an operator to the dead name.

item: hook-flags.sh as a live goal defect
reason: The POSIX mirror carries no canonical-name overrides (shared/README.md:72), so hook_enabled goal would consult the derived SYSTEM_GOAL_DISABLED; but every live consumer (git-live-follow.sh:161-162, check-git-hooks.sh:42/:117, git-primary-reconcile.sh:177, worktree-guard.sh, session-cleanup.sh, pre-commit) asks about git/session concerns, so no goal surface is affected. Latent, recorded so ring 5 does not re-derive it as a bug.

item: The hub matrix's '| goal |, by-design:' comma as a goal-specific defect
reason: The same comment-folded rendering appears in every by-design cell of every row (codex-watchdog, dist-freshness, permission-policy, session-lifecycle); it is the table's convention.

item: dispatch-guard.cjs referencing opencode-goal.js as a coupling defect
reason: Both mentions are explicit comments about mirroring the goal plugin's sweep/archive/prune pattern and tuning (:52-55, :420); textual inspiration, not a live dependency.

item: goal.md scaffold and metadata surfaces as new defects
reason: template-structure.js:64/:202, graph-metadata-parser.ts:58, check-template-staleness.sh:177, create.sh and the template README/EXTENSION-GUIDE rows are consistent with ring 3's lazy-addon finding; tests pin the scaffold shape (scaffold-golden-snapshots.vitest.ts:82, :122-141; template-version-parity.vitest.ts:78-80).

item: ENV-REFERENCE.md's plugin-section omission of OPENCODE_GOAL_STATE_DIR as a contradiction
reason: The section is scoped to plugin-consumed variables and the plugin deliberately ignores the state-dir override (R2-F2). It is a roster gap for the core's variables, recorded in iteration 4 section 4, not a contradiction: ENV-REFERENCE:83 states the flag pair itself correctly.

item: goal-file-manifest.txt as part of the session-goal system
reason: deep-review-auto.yaml:373-376 parses it as one repo-relative file path per line for review scope; it is a review manifest (recorded under R4-F10 as a naming collision, not a goal-system surface).
